poems.title: Bloodline
poems.note: the plain beside the Avenue of the Dead — the ancestors' parade

set_pieces.name: The field goes still
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · A The field goes still — “They tell me to ask if I can inherit the earth”

set_pieces.name: Naming stars
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · B Naming stars — “name my own stars”

set_pieces.name: Southern-pine basement (memory)
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · C Southern-pine basement (memory) — “humid basements as bedrooms”

set_pieces.name: Universes and blessings
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · D Universes and blessings — “invent a new universe”

set_pieces.name: Blood through the hands
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · E Blood through the hands — “their blood flows through my hands”

set_pieces.name: Baritone and warning
set_pieces.line: 5 BLOODLINE · F Baritone and warning — “deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries”

foundry_refs.desc: In the still night, POET enters a vibrant, welcoming parade of afro-futuristic ancestors who bestow stars, galaxies, and universes upon him.
POET finds and reattaches hands, then stands contemplatively in the field.
Literal visual match: Profile view showing glowing cervical spine and ribcage pulsating with amber heat.
foundry_refs.line: Coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where Southern pine could comfort my spine.

foundry_refs.line: Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.
